content.title: About
content.content: Mustard is a condiment made from ground mustard seeds (Sinapis alba, Brassica juncea and others), water, vinegar, salt and sometimes sugar or spices. It has a sharp, slightly bitter taste and a distinctive aroma that develops with aging.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mustard seeds have been used in cooking and medicine since ancient Egypt.
There are several types of mustard: yellow (made from white mustard), spicy (from brown mustard) and Dijon (from black mustard with wine vinegar).
Mustard powder changes colour with pH: it stays yellow in acidic environments and turns brown in alkaline ones.
In Japan, a fermented mustard paste called "massa-go" is a popular specialty.
Mustard often acts as a natural preservative because of its antibacterial properties.

items.title: Rich in glucosinolates
items.content: Glucosinolates have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory effects, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium in mustard helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Mustard seeds stimulate bile production, improving fat digestion.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Despite its strong flavor, mustard is low‑calorie, making it a diet‑friendly addition.

items.title: Source of omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Some mustard varieties contain alpha‑linolenic acid, beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mustard seeds, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Very spicy mustard can irritate the stomach and intestinal lining, especially in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Mustard may enhance the effects of anticoagulant medications, so moderation is advised for those on blood thinners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use mustard as a topping for meats, fish, cheeses, in sauces, marinades and salad dressings. It can be added to sandwiches, hot dogs, potato dishes, or used as a base for barbecue sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store mustard in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator. At room temperature it lasts several weeks, but in the fridge it can keep for up to a year. Keep it away from moisture and direct light.
